1.q: What is the main difference between AutoTrim and TimeBolt?
1.a: The workflow. TimeBolt imports and processes one clip at a time and exports one XML per clip, which you then have to merge manually in your editor. AutoTrim takes the whole batch at once, processes clips in parallel and exports a single, already-assembled XML or FCPXML timeline. On a six-clip shoot, that's the difference between assembling six timelines by hand and importing one.

2.q: Does TimeBolt merge all clips into a single timeline?
2.a: No. TimeBolt exports one XML file per clip, and you have to merge them manually in Final Cut Pro, Premiere Pro or Resolve. AutoTrim exports one merged timeline for the entire batch, already in order and ready to edit.

3.q: How much faster is AutoTrim than cutting silences manually?
3.a: In a measured real-world case, cleaning 30 minutes of talking-head footage took about 48 minutes with manual razor cuts and about 1 minute with AutoTrim — roughly 48× faster, or 96% of rough-cut time saved.

4.q: Does AutoTrim work with Final Cut Pro?

0.q: Does Final Cut Pro have a built-in silence remover?
0.a: No. As of 2026, Final Cut Pro has no native feature that detects and removes silences, and no plugin marketplace to add one. Silences have to be cut manually with the blade tool — or removed automatically with a standalone app like AutoTrim, which exports an FCPXML timeline straight back into FCP.

1.q: How do I remove silences in Final Cut Pro automatically?
1.a: Use a standalone tool that processes your clips before they reach FCP. With AutoTrim: drag all your clips into the app, pick a preset (YouTube, Podcast or Vlog) or adjust the silence threshold and padding, preview the cuts, then export one FCPXML timeline and import it into Final Cut Pro. Cleaning 30 minutes of footage takes about 1 minute.

2.q: Can Final Cut Pro remove filler words like "um" and "uh"?
2.a: Not natively — FCP has no transcription-based editing. AutoTrim detects filler words and hesitations using local AI transcription and can cut them automatically. The feature is still experimental, and results vary with language and diction.

3.q: Why is there no silence-removal plugin for Final Cut Pro?
3.a: Final Cut Pro supports effects plugins (FxPlug), but not workflow plugins that could analyze footage and cut your timeline — which is why tools like AutoCut exist for Premiere Pro and DaVinci Resolve but not for FCP. The established workaround is a standalone app that generates an FCPXML timeline, which is exactly what AutoTrim does.

4.a: In a measured real-world case, about 48 minutes of blade-tool work for 30 minutes of talking-head footage. AutoTrim processed the same footage in about 1 minute — roughly 48× faster, 96% of rough-cut time saved.

silences.title: Silences go first.
silences.body: The threshold sets itself for each file. A margin is kept on either side of a sentence, so a cut never clips the first or last syllable. On an hour of talking-head footage, a third of it is silence.

hesitations.title: Um.
hesitations.body: A model trained to spot hesitations, not a transcript bent to the task: it hears the drawn-out "uhh", the "hmm", the word picked up again. Every hesitation is marked on the timeline, you see it, you hear it, it goes. All on your machine, nothing uploaded.
hesitations.proof: 123 hesitations removed from the real hour

multicam.title: Three cameras, two mics, one drop.
multicam.body: Drop every file of one take. They find each other by their sound and line up to the frame, even when a camera started late, split into two files or drifts. One mic per person: a cut only when nobody speaks, never two voices at once, and one person's "um" only goes if the other is silent. The edit follows who's talking, wide shot when everyone does.

multicam.truth: The exported timeline stacks the angles: V1 for the main angle, the others above it, one track per mic, all cut at the same instants. In Resolve, Final Cut and Premiere.

items.q: Final Cut Pro, Premiere Pro, DaVinci Resolve?
items.a: Yes: FCPXML for Final Cut Pro and Resolve, XML for Premiere Pro. One timeline, all your files end to end, every clip with its handles.

items.q: Do my files leave my computer?
items.a: No, never. The models download once, then everything happens on your machine, even offline.

items.q: What if it cuts too much?
items.a: The preview shows three states, kept, silence, hesitation, and you can listen to what was removed. Adjust the threshold, run again, then export: every cut stays editable in your editing software.

items.q: My podcast has one mic per person?
items.a: Yes. AutoTrim only cuts when nobody speaks, never two voices at once, and one person's "um" only goes if the other is silent.
Drop every file of one take: they line up to the frame by their sound. The timeline stacks the angles, and the preview shows the edit following who's talking.

items.q: Which languages are hesitations detected in?
items.a: About ten languages, including English and French. Silences have no language.

items.q: Screen recordings (OBS, VLC, QuickTime), variable frame rate?
items.a: Supported. The real duration is kept, so the timeline lands right.
Take the video already cut, one MP4 per source. For CapCut, one numbered clip per cut, to drop in order.
Yes, same processing. Export as AAC or as a timeline.

items.q: What does the free version include?
items.a: Everything, with no time limit: silences, hesitations, multicam, preview. Only the export needs a licence.

items.q: How many machines, and what if it's not for me?
items.a: Two machines per licence. Refunded within 14 days, no questions asked.
